sentences.zh: 陳邦瞻，字德遠，高安人。

translations.literal: Chen Bangzhan, styled Deyuan, was a native of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bangzhan, whose style was Deyuan, came from Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京大理寺評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewing officer at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviewing officer at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 歷南京吏部郎中，出為浙江參政。

translations.literal: He served as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and then went out as administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, he was posted abroad as administrative commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 進福建按察使，遷右布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian and then transferred to right provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to surveillance commissioner of Fujian and was then made right provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 改補河南，分理彰德諸府。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Henan and put in charge of the prefectures around Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to Henan, he took charge of the prefectures in the Zhangde region.

sentences.zh: 開水田千頃，建滏陽書院，集諸生講習。

translations.literal: He opened a thousand qing of paddy fields, built the Fuyang Academy, and gathered students for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed a thousand qing of paddy land, founded the Fuyang Academy, and gathered students there for study.

sentences.zh: 士民祠祀之。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners enshrined him in a temple.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry and commoners erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 就改左布政使，以右副都御史巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: He was then made left provincial administration commissioner and, as right vice censor-in-chief, became grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left provincial administration commissioner and appointed grand coordinator of Shaanxi with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上林土官黃德勛弟德隆及子祚允叛德勛，投田州土酋岑茂仁。

translations.literal: The native official Huang Dexun of Shanglin had a younger brother Delong and a son Zuoyun who rebelled against Dexun and went over to the Tujia chieftain Cen Maoren of Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dexun, the native official of Shanglin, was betrayed by his younger brother Delong and his son Zuoyun, who defected to Cen Maoren, the tribal chief of Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 茂仁納之，襲破上林，殺德勛，掠妻子金帛。

translations.literal: Maoren received them, stormed and broke Shanglin, killed Dexun, and plundered his wife, children, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Maoren took them in, overran Shanglin, killed Dexun, and carried off his family, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 守臣問狀，詭言德勛病亡，乞以祚允繼。

translations.literal: When defending officials inquired into the affair, they falsely reported that Dexun had died of illness and asked that Zuoyun succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials investigated, they falsely claimed Dexun had died of illness and petitioned that Zuoyun succeed him.

sentences.zh: 邦瞻請討於朝。

translations.literal: Bangzhan requested a punitive campaign from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzhan asked the court to send a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 會光宗嗣位，即擢邦瞻兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務兼巡撫廣東，遂移師討擒之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, Bangzhan was at once promoted to right vice minister of War, made supreme commander of the Two Guangs with concurrent grand coordination of Guangdong, and then moved his army to campaign and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, Bangzhan was promptly made right vice minister of War and supreme commander of the Two Guangs, with concurrent duties as grand coordinator of Guangdong; he then marched his forces out and captured the rebels.

sentences.zh: 海寇林莘老嘯聚萬余人侵掠海濱，邦瞻扼之，不得逞。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Lin Xin gathered more than ten thousand men and raided the coast; Bangzhan blocked him so that he could not carry out his designs.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Lin Xin rallied more than ten thousand men to raid the coast, but Bangzhan hemmed him in and kept him from acting.

sentences.zh: 澳夷築室青州，奸民與通，時侵內地，邦瞻燔其巢。

translations.literal: Foreigners from Macao built houses at Qingzhou; scoundrels colluded with them and from time to time raided the interior, and Bangzhan burned their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Macao foreigners built settlements at Qingzhou, and local ruffians who dealt with them periodically raided inland; Bangzhan burned out their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 召拜工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed right vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed right vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未上，改兵部，進左。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and promoted to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed office, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年五月疏陳四事，中言：「客氏既出復入，乃陛下過舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Tianqi he memorialized on four matters, saying among other things: "That Nurse Ke was expelled and then brought back in was a mistaken act on Your Majesty's part.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Tianqi he submitted a memorial on four matters, writing in part: "That Nurse Ke was sent away and then brought back was a mistake on Your Majesty's part.

sentences.zh: 輔臣不封還內降，引義固爭，致罪謫言者，再蹈拒諫之失，其何解於人言？」

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not seal and return the inner rescript, but held fast to principle in remonstrance, yet caused remonstrators to be punished and banished—again committing the fault of rejecting remonstrance; how can this be explained to public opinion?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chief ministers did not seal and return the inner rescript, and though they argued on principle, they allowed remonstrators to be punished and banished—once again refusing counsel. How can this be squared with public opinion?

sentences.zh: 疏入，忤旨譙讓。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it offended the throne and he was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, it drew an imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 尋兼戶、工二部侍郎，專理軍需。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he concurrently held the vice ministerships of Revenue and Works, with sole charge of military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent appointments as vice minister of Revenue and of Works, with sole responsibility for military supplies.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官，詔贈尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office, and an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office, and the throne posthumously granted him the rank of minister.

sentences.zh: 邦瞻好學，敦風節。

translations.literal: Bangzhan loved learning and upheld integrity of character.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzhan was devoted to learning and steadfast in moral principle.

sentences.zh: 服官三十年，吏議不及。

translations.literal: In thirty years of office, no censorial criticism ever touched him.
translations.idiomatic: Through thirty years of service, no official censure ever touched him.

sentences.zh: 畢懋康，字孟侯，歙人。

translations.literal: Bi Maokang, styled Menghou, was a native of She.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Maokang, whose style was Menghou, came from She county.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 以中書舍人授御史。

translations.literal: From the post of secretary in the Secretariat he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as a secretarial draftsman, he was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 言內閣不當專用詞臣，邊臣失律者宜重按，部郎田大年、賀盛瑞，中書舍人丁元薦以忤權要廢，當雪，疏留中。

translations.literal: He said that the Grand Secretariat should not employ literary officials exclusively, that frontier officials who violated discipline should be sternly investigated, and that the department directors Tian Danian and He Shengrui and the secretarial draftsman Ding Yuanjian, who had been dismissed for offending powerful figures, ought to be cleared—the memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Grand Secretariat should not rely exclusively on literary officials, that delinquent frontier commanders deserved stern investigation, and that the dismissed officials Tian Danian, He Shengrui, and Ding Yuanjian—punished for offending the powerful—ought to be rehabilitated; the memorial was held at court.

sentences.zh: 視鹽長蘆。

translations.literal: He inspected the salt administration of Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to inspect the Changlu salt administration.

sentences.zh: 畿輔多河渠，湮廢不治。

translations.literal: In the capital region there were many rivers and canals that had silted up and fallen into disrepair.
translations.idiomatic: Many rivers and canals in the capital region had silted up and been left unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 懋康言：「保定清河，其源發於滿城，抵清苑而南十里，則湯家口為上閘，又十里則清楊為下閘，順流東下，直抵天津。

translations.literal: Maokang said: "The Qing River of Baoding rises at Mancheng; ten li south of Qingyuan, Tangjiakou is the upper lock, and ten li farther on Qingyang is the lower lock; flowing east with the current, it reaches Tianjin directly.
translations.idiomatic: Maokang wrote: "The Qing River in Baoding rises at Mancheng; ten li south of Qingyuan, Tangjiakou forms the upper lock, and ten li farther on, Qingyang is the lower lock. Following the current eastward, it runs straight to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 旁近易、安諸州，新安、雄、完、唐、慶都諸縣，並通舟楫仰其利。

translations.literal: The nearby prefectures of Yi and An and the counties of Xin'an, Xiong, Wan, Tang, and Qingdu all could use boats and depend on its benefits.
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring prefectures of Yi and An and the counties of Xin'an, Xiong, Wan, Tang, and Qingdu could all navigate it and share in its benefits.

sentences.zh: 二閘創自永樂初，日久頹圮，急宜修復，歲漕臨、德二倉二十萬石餉保定、易州、紫荊諸軍，足使士卒宿飽。

translations.literal: The two locks were first built in the early Yongle reign and had long since fallen into ruin; they urgently needed repair. Each year two hundred thousand shi of grain could be transported by canal from the Lin and De granaries to supply the armies at Baoding, Yizhou, Zijing, and elsewhere, enough to keep the troops fully provisioned.
translations.idiomatic: The two locks were built early in the Yongle reign but had long since crumbled and urgently needed repair. Two hundred thousand shi of grain could be shipped yearly from the Lin and De granaries to supply the garrisons at Baoding, Yizhou, and Zijing, keeping the troops fully fed.

sentences.zh: 往者，密雲、昌平故不通漕，萬歷初，總督劉應節、楊兆疏潮、白二河，陵泉諸水，漕粟以餉二鎮，二鎮之軍賴之。

translations.literal: Formerly Miyun and Changping had had no canal transport; at the beginning of Wanli the supreme commanders Liu Yingjie and Yang Zhao dredged the Chao and Bai rivers and the waters of Lingquan, transported grain by canal to supply the two garrisons, and the troops of the two garrisons relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Miyun and Changping once had no canal access; at the start of the Wanli reign, supreme commanders Liu Yingjie and Yang Zhao dredged the Chao and Bai rivers and the Lingquan waters and shipped grain to both garrisons, on which their troops depended.

sentences.zh: 此可仿而行也。」

translations.literal: This may be imitated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The same approach can be followed here.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 巡按陜西，疏陳邊政十事，劾罷副總兵王學書等七人。

translations.literal: As touring censor of Shaanxi, he memorialized on ten matters of frontier administration and impeached and removed seven men including the vice commander Wang Xueshu.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Shaanxi as censor, he submitted ten proposals on frontier policy and secured the dismissal of seven officials, including vice commander Wang Xueshu.

sentences.zh: 請建宗學如郡縣學制，報可。

translations.literal: He asked to establish a princely academy on the model of the prefectural and county schools, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to establish a princely academy modeled on the prefectural and county schools, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 改按山東，擢順天府丞，以憂去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tour Shandong, was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian, and left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shandong as touring censor, he was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian but left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年起右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was recalled as right vice censor-in-chief to pacify and administer Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was recalled as right vice censor-in-chief to administer Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 懋康雅負器局，揚歷中外，與族兄懋良並有清譽，稱「二畢」。

translations.literal: Maokang was by nature endowed with capacity and vision; he served widely at court and in the provinces, and he and his clansman Maoliang both enjoyed a reputation for integrity, being called "the two Bis."
translations.idiomatic: Maokang was a man of real capacity who served widely at court and abroad; he and his kinsman Maoliang both enjoyed reputations for integrity and were known as "the two Bis."

sentences.zh: 懋良，字師臯。

translations.literal: Maoliang, styled Shigao.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang, whose style was Shigao,

sentences.zh: 先懋康舉進士。

translations.literal: passed the jinshi examination before Maokang.
translations.idiomatic: had passed the jinshi examination before Maokang.

sentences.zh: 由萬載知縣擢南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Wanzai he was promoted to secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate of Wanzai to a secretaryship in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷副使，至左布政使，俱在福建。

translations.literal: He served as vice commissioner and rose to left provincial administration commissioner, all in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served through vice commissioner up to left provincial administration commissioner, all in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 振饑民，減加派，撫降海寇，以善績稱。

translations.literal: He relieved famine victims, reduced surtax levies, pacified surrendered sea bandits, and was praised for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved famine victims, cut supplemental levies, pacified surrendered pirates, and won praise for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 懋康為巡撫之歲，懋良亦自順天府尹擢戶部右侍郎，督倉場。

translations.literal: In the year when Maokang was grand coordinator, Maoliang too was promoted from prefect of Shuntian to right vice minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The year Maokang became grand coordinator, Maoliang was promoted from prefect of Shuntian to right vice minister of Revenue in charge of the granaries.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢以懋康為趙南星所引，欲去之。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian, because Maokang had been brought forward by Zhao Nanxing, wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Maokang had been promoted by Zhao Nanxing, Wei Zhongxian sought to remove him.

sentences.zh: 御史王際逵劾其附麗邪黨，遂削籍。

translations.literal: The censor Wang Jikui impeached him for clinging to an evil faction, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jikui impeached him for siding with a corrupt faction, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 而懋良亦以不附忠賢，為御史張訥所論，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Maoliang too, for not siding with Zhongxian, was attacked by the censor Zhang Ne and dismissed to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang, for refusing to align with Zhongxian, was denounced by Censor Zhang Ne and dismissed to private life.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相繼去國，士論更以為榮。

translations.literal: The brothers left office in succession, and public opinion regarded this all the more as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers left office in succession, and public opinion held it all the more honorable.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起懋康南京通政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, Maokang was recalled as transmission commissioner at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign, Maokang was recalled as transmission commissioner at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 越二年，召拜兵部右侍郎，尋罷。

translations.literal: Two years later he was summoned as right vice minister of War, but was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was summoned as right vice minister of War but was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而懋良亦起兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Maoliang too was raised to left vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang was also appointed left vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 會京師戒嚴，尚書張鳳翔以下皆獲罪，懋良得原，致仕去。

translations.literal: When the capital was placed under martial law, the minister Zhang Fengxiang and those below him were all punished; Maoliang was pardoned and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was placed under martial law, Minister Zhang Fengxiang and his subordinates were all punished; Maoliang was pardoned and retired.

sentences.zh: 懋康再起南京戶部右侍郎，督糧儲。

translations.literal: Maokang was again raised as right vice minister of Revenue at Nanjing to supervise grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Maokang was again appointed right vice minister of Revenue at Nanjing to oversee grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 旋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆卒於家。

translations.literal: Both brothers died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers died at home.

sentences.zh: 蕭近高，字抑之，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingao, styled Yizhi, was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingao, whose style was Yizhi, came from Luling.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretarial draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretarial draftsman.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 甫拜官，即上疏言罷礦稅、釋系囚、起廢棄三事，明詔已頒，不可中止。

translations.literal: As soon as he took office he memorialized on three matters—abolishing mining taxes, releasing prisoners, and recalling the dismissed—saying that clear edicts had already been issued and must not be halted.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office, he memorialized urging the abolition of mining taxes, the release of prisoners, and the recall of dismissed officials, arguing that clear edicts had already been issued and must not be reversed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪俸一年。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped him of salary for one year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and suspended his salary for a year.

sentences.zh: 頃之，論江西稅使潘相擅刑宗人罪，不報。

translations.literal: Before long he spoke on the crime of Pan Xiang, the Jiangxi tax commissioner, in arbitrarily punishing a member of the imperial clan; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he denounced Pan Xiang, the Jiangxi tax commissioner, for unlawfully punishing a member of the imperial clan; the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 既而停礦分稅之詔下，相失利，擅移駐景德鎮，請專理窯務。

translations.literal: Later, when the edict halting mines and dividing tax receipts was issued, Xiang lost revenue; on his own authority he moved his station to Jingdezhen and asked to manage the kilns exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict later halted mining and divided tax receipts, Xiang lost revenue; he moved on his own authority to Jingdezhen and asked to oversee the porcelain kilns exclusively.

sentences.zh: 帝即可之，近高復力爭。

translations.literal: The emperor at once approved it, and Jingao again argued strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly approved, and Jingao protested again with force.

sentences.zh: 後江西撫按並劾相，相以為近高主之，疏詆甚力。

translations.literal: Later the Jiangxi governor and surveillance commissioner jointly impeached Xiang; Xiang thought Jingao was behind it and memorialized in fierce denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Jiangxi governor and surveillance commissioner jointly impeached Xiang, who believed Jingao was behind it and attacked him fiercely in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 近高疏辨，復劾相。

translations.literal: Jingao memorialized in his own defense and again impeached Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingao defended himself in a memorial and again impeached Xiang.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，相不久自引去。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not acted on, Xiang before long withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Though the memorial went unanswered, Xiang soon withdrew on his own.

sentences.zh: 屢遷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he became chief supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to chief supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 知縣滿朝薦、諸生王大義等皆忤中使，系獄三年。

translations.literal: The magistrate Man Chaojian, the student Wang Dayi, and others had all offended eunuch agents and had been imprisoned for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Man Chaojian, student Wang Dayi, and others had offended eunuch agents and languished in prison for three years.

sentences.zh: 近高請釋之，不報。

translations.literal: Jingao asked that they be released; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Jingao petitioned for their release, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 遼東稅使高淮激民變，近高劾其罪，請撤還，帝不納。

translations.literal: Gao Huai, the Liaodong tax commissioner, provoked a popular uprising; Jingao impeached his crimes and asked that he be recalled, but the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huai, the Liaodong tax commissioner, provoked a popular uprising; Jingao impeached him and asked that he be recalled, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又以淮誣奏逮同知王邦才、參將李獲陽，近高復論救。

translations.literal: When Huai also had the vice prefect Wang Bangcai and the regional commander Li Huoyang arrested on false charges, Jingao again pleaded for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai had Vice Prefect Wang Bangcai and Regional Commander Li Huoyang arrested on false charges, Jingao again pleaded for them.

sentences.zh: 會廷臣多劾淮者，帝不得已征還，而邦才等系如故。

translations.literal: When many court officials impeached Huai, the emperor had no choice but to recall him, yet Bangcai and the others remained imprisoned as before.
translations.idiomatic: When many court officials impeached Huai, the emperor had no choice but to recall him, yet Wang Bangcai and the others remained in custody.

sentences.zh: 無何，極陳言路不通、耳目壅蔽之患。

translations.literal: Before long he set forth at length the evils of a blocked remonstrance channel and obstructed ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he spoke at length about the dangers of a blocked remonstrance channel and stifled intelligence reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又言王錫爵密揭行私，宜止勿召；

translations.literal: Not long after, he again said that Wang Xijue had used secret memorials to pursue private ends and ought not to be summoned again;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he argued that Wang Xijue had used secret memorials for private ends and should not be recalled;

sentences.zh: 朱賡被彈六十余疏，不當更留。

translations.literal: Zhu Geng had been impeached in more than sixty memorials and ought not to be kept on further.
translations.idiomatic: and that Zhu Geng, impeached in more than sixty memorials, ought not to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None of these received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these petitions received a response.

sentences.zh: 故事，六科都給事中內外遞轉。

translations.literal: By precedent the chief supervising secretaries of the Six Sections rotated between inner and outer service.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the chief supervising secretaries of the Six Sections rotated between capital and provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 人情輕外，率規避，近高自請外補。

translations.literal: People generally looked down on outer posts and usually tried to avoid them; Jingao himself asked for an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials disdained provincial posts and tried to avoid them, but Jingao volunteered for provincial service.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎楊時喬請亟許以成其美。

translations.literal: Yang Shiqiao, vice minister of Personnel, asked that he be quickly granted this to complete his fine purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao urged that the request be granted promptly to honor his integrity.

sentences.zh: 乃用為浙江右參政，進按察使。

translations.literal: He was then appointed right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang and promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang and promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以病歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 起浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: He was recalled as left provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as left provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 所至以清操聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 白瑜，字紹明，永平人。

translations.literal: Bai Yu, styled Shaoming, was a native of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yu, whose style was Shaoming, came from Yongping.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed supervising secretary of the War Section.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed supervising secretary in the War Section.

sentences.zh: 帝既冊立東宮，上太后徽號，瑜請推廣孝慈，以敦儉、持廉、惜人才、省冤獄四事進，皆引《祖訓》及先朝事以規時政，辭甚切。

translations.literal: After the emperor had invested the heir apparent and bestowed an honorific title on the empress dowager, Yu asked that filial piety and compassion be extended further, advancing four matters—practicing frugality, upholding integrity, cherishing talent, and reducing wrongful imprisonment—all citing the Ancestral Injunctions and precedents of earlier reigns to admonish current policy; his language was very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent was invested and the empress dowager was given an honorific title, Yu urged the extension of filial devotion and compassion, proposing frugality, integrity, cherishing talent, and reducing wrongful imprisonment—citing the Ancestral Injunctions and earlier precedents to admonish current policy in forceful terms.

sentences.zh: 三十年，京師旱，陜西河南黃河竭。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year there was drought in the capital, and the Yellow River dried up in Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, the capital suffered drought, and the Yellow River ran dry in Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 禮官請修省，瑜言：「修省宜行實政。

translations.literal: The ritual officials asked for repentance and self-examination; Yu said: "Repentance should be carried out through real policies.
translations.idiomatic: When the ritual officials called for repentance and self-examination, Yu wrote: "Repentance must take the form of real policy.

sentences.zh: 今逐臣久錮，累臣久羈，一蒙矜釋，即可感格天心。」

translations.literal: Now banished officials have long been imprisoned and convicted officials long detained; once they receive compassionate release, Heaven's mind can at once be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Banished officials have long been imprisoned and convicted men long held in custody; a single act of mercy would move Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 末言礦稅之害。

translations.literal: At the end he spoke of the harm of mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He ended by denouncing the harm of mining taxes.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these petitions received a response.

sentences.zh: 累遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he became chief supervising secretary of the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary of the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 帝於射場營乾德臺，瑜抗疏力諫，又再疏請斥中官王朝、陳永壽，帝不能無憾。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Qiande Terrace at the archery ground; Yu submitted a forceful memorial in protest and again memorialized asking that the eunuchs Wang Chao and Chen Yongshou be expelled; the emperor could not but harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor built the Qiande Terrace at the archery ground, Yu protested in a forceful memorial and twice asked that eunuchs Wang Chao and Chen Yongshou be expelled; the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 會瑜論治河當專任，遂責其剿拾陳言，謫廣西布政使照磨。

translations.literal: When Yu happened to discuss river control and said a single official should be given sole responsibility, he was charged with cobbling together stale words and banished to assistant registrar in the Guangxi provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu argued that river control required a dedicated commissioner, he was accused of recycling platitudes and demoted to assistant registrar in the Guangxi provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起光祿少卿，三遷太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Yu was raised as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was transferred three times to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, Yu was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and rose through three posts to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 給事中倪思輝、朱欽相，御史王心一以直言被謫，瑜抗疏論救。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Ni Sihui and Zhu Qinxiang and the censor Wang Xinyi were banished for outspoken remonstrance; Yu submitted a forceful memorial pleading for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Ni Sihui and Zhu Qinxiang and Censor Wang Xinyi were banished for outspoken remonstrance; Yu submitted a forceful memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，由通政使拜刑部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, from transmission commissioner he was appointed right vice minister of Justice and directed ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was appointed right vice minister of Justice from his post as transmission commissioner and directed ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃兄子養性奉詔還籍，逗遛不去，其家奴張應登訐其通塞外。

translations.literal: Yangxing, a nephew of Consort Zheng, had been ordered by edict to return to his native place but lingered and would not leave; his household slave Zhang Yingdeng accused him of communicating with foreigners beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing, a nephew of Consort Zheng, had been ordered home by edict but lingered on; his household slave Zhang Yingdeng accused him of dealing with foreigners beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 永寧伯王天瑞者，顯皇后弟也，以後故銜鄭氏，遂偕其弟錦衣天麟交章劾養性不軌。

translations.literal: Wang Tianrui, Baron of Yongning, was the younger brother of Empress Xian; because of the empress he bore a grudge against the Zheng clan and, together with his younger brother Tianlin of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, submitted successive memorials impeaching Yangxing for disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tianrui, Baron of Yongning, was the younger brother of Empress Xian; resenting the Zheng clan because of the empress, he and his younger brother Tianlin of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard jointly impeached Yangxing for treasonable conduct.

sentences.zh: 瑜以鄭氏得罪先朝，而交通事實誣，乃會都御史趙南星、大理卿陳於廷等讞上其獄，請抵奴誣告罪，勒養性居遠方。

translations.literal: Yu held that the Zheng clan had offended the previous reign and that the charge of illicit communication was false; he joined the censor-in-chief Zhao Nanxing, the chief justice Chen Yuting, and others in reporting the case for judgment, asking that the slave be punished for false accusation and that Yangxing be compelled to live in a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Yu held that the Zheng clan had already been punished in the previous reign and that the charge of illicit communication was fabricated; joining Censor-in-Chief Zhao Nanxing and Chief Justice Chen Yuting, he reported the case for judgment, asked that the slave be punished for false accusation, and required Yangxing to live in exile.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Imperial approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 明年進左侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of minister.

sentences.zh: 程紹，字公業，德州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Shao, styled Gongye, was a native of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shao, whose style was Gongye, came from Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 祖瑤，江西右布政使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao was right provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao had served as right provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 紹舉萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: Shao passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Shao received his jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除汝寧推官，征授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Runing and was summoned as supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Runing, then summoned as supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 巡視京營。

translations.literal: He inspected the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to inspect the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 副將佟養正等五人行賄求遷，皆劾置於理。

translations.literal: The vice generals Tong Yangzheng and four others tried to bribe their way to promotion; he impeached them all and had them handed over for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Vice generals Tong Yangzheng and four others tried to bribe their way to promotion; he impeached them all and had them prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使采礦河南，紹兩疏言宜罷，皆不報。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to mine in Henan; Shao twice memorialized that this should be stopped, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent envoys to open mines in Henan, Shao twice memorialized that the practice should cease; both petitions went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to left supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 會大計京官，御史許聞造訐戶部侍郎張養蒙等，語侵吏部侍郎裴應章。

translations.literal: At the great evaluation of capital officials, the censor Xu Wenzao denounced the vice minister of Revenue Zhang Yangmeng and others, his language impugning the vice minister of Personnel Pei Yingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: During the great evaluation of capital officials, Censor Xu Wenzao denounced Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Yangmeng and others in language that also impugned Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Yingzhang.

sentences.zh: 紹言聞造挾吏部以避計典，且附會閣臣張位，聞造乃貶邊方。

translations.literal: Shao said that Wenzao was using the Ministry of Personnel to evade the evaluation and was moreover aligning himself with Grand Secretary Zhang Wei; Wenzao was then banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shao argued that Wenzao was manipulating the Ministry of Personnel to evade evaluation and was aligning himself with Grand Secretary Zhang Wei; Wenzao was banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 主事趙世德考察貶官，廷議征楊應龍，兵部舉世德知兵，紹駁止之。

translations.literal: The director Zhao Shide was demoted in the evaluation; when the court debated campaigning against Yang Yinglong, the Ministry of War recommended Shide as knowing warfare, and Shao refuted this and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhao Shide was demoted in the evaluation; when the court debated campaigning against Yang Yinglong, the Ministry of War recommended Shide as militarily capable, but Shao blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 又劾文選郎楊守峻，守峻自引去。

translations.literal: He also impeached the selection director Yang Shoujun, who withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Selection Director Yang Shoujun, who resigned on his own.

sentences.zh: 饒州通判沈榜貶官，夤緣稅監潘相得留，紹極言非法。

translations.literal: Shen Bang, vice prefect of Raozhou, had been demoted but, through connections with the tax commissioner Pan Xiang, was allowed to remain; Shao spoke forcefully that this was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bang, vice prefect of Raozhou, had been demoted but remained in office through connections with tax commissioner Pan Xiang; Shao protested that this was unlawful.

sentences.zh: 山西稅使張忠以夏縣知縣韓薰忤己，奏調之僻地，紹又爭之，帝怒，斥為民。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong, the Shanxi tax commissioner, because the magistrate of Xia county Han Xun had offended him, memorialized to transfer him to a remote place; Shao again contested this; the emperor was angry and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong, the Shanxi tax commissioner, had Magistrate Han Xun of Xia county transferred to a remote post because Han had offended him; when Shao protested again, the emperor angrily stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 以沈一貫救，詔鐫一秩，出之外。

translations.literal: Because Shen Yiguan interceded, an edict reduced him one rank and sent him outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Yiguan interceded, an edict reduced his rank by one step and sent him out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中李應策、御史李炳等爭之，帝益怒，並薰斥為民，而奪應策等俸。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Li Yingce, the censor Li Bing, and others contested this; the emperor grew angrier, dismissed both Xun and them to commoner status, and stripped Yingce and the others of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Yingce, Censor Li Bing, and others protested; the emperor grew angrier, dismissed both Han Xun and the protesters from office, and suspended their salaries.

sentences.zh: 紹家居二十年。

translations.literal: Shao lived at home for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Shao lived in retirement for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，起太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was raised as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，歷右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he served as right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqi he became right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 宗室居儀封者為盜窟，紹列上其狀，廢徙高墻。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen living at Yifeng were a nest of bandits; Shao listed their condition and had them deposed and moved to the high wall.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen at Yifeng had become a nest of bandits; Shao reported their crimes and had them deposed and confined to the high wall.

sentences.zh: 臨漳民耕地漳濱，得玉璽，龍紐龜形，方四寸，厚三寸，文曰：「受命於天，既壽永昌」，以獻紹。

translations.literal: A commoner of Linzhang farming by the Zhang River bank found a jade seal with a dragon knob in tortoise form, four inches square and three inches thick, inscribed "Receiving the Mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity," and presented it to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: A farmer of Linzhang working along the Zhang River found a jade seal with a dragon knob in tortoise form, four inches square and three inches thick, inscribed "Receiving the Mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity," and presented it to Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹聞之於朝，略言：「秦璽不足征久矣。

translations.literal: Shao reported it to the court, saying in brief: "The Qin seal has long ceased to be proof of anything.
translations.idiomatic: Shao reported the find to court, writing in part: "The Qin imperial seal has long ceased to be meaningful proof.

sentences.zh: 今璽出，適在臣疆，既不當復埋地下，又不合私秘人間。

translations.literal: Now that the seal has appeared, and it happens to be within my jurisdiction, it is neither fitting to bury it in the ground again nor proper to keep it secretly among men.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this seal has appeared within my jurisdiction, it should neither be buried again nor kept secretly in private hands.

sentences.zh: 欲遣官恭進闕廷，跡涉貢媚。

translations.literal: To send an official to present it respectfully at court would smack of flattery.
translations.idiomatic: To dispatch an official to present it respectfully at court would look like flattery.

sentences.zh: 且至尊所寶，在德不在璽，故先馳奏聞，候命進止。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the sovereign should treasure is virtue, not a seal; therefore I first dispatch this report and await orders on how to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what the sovereign should treasure is virtue, not a seal; I therefore report first and await your orders.

sentences.zh: 昔王孫圉不寶玉珩，齊威王不寶照乘，前史美之。

translations.literal: Formerly Prince Sun Yu did not treasure the jade tablet, and King Wei of Qi did not treasure the luminous carriage; earlier histories praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sun Yu of Chu did not treasure a jade tablet, and King Wei of Qi did not treasure a luminous carriage—earlier histories praised such restraint.

sentences.zh: 陛下尊賢愛士，野無留良。

translations.literal: Your Majesty honors the worthy and cherishes scholars, yet no worthy man is left in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty honors the worthy and cherishes scholars, yet worthy men still languish unused in retirement.

sentences.zh: 尚有一代名賢，如鄒元標、馮從吾、王紀、周嘉謨、盛以弘、孫慎行、鐘羽正、余懋衡、曹於汴等皆憂國奉公，白首魁艾。

translations.literal: There remain famous worthies of the age, such as Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Wang Ji, Zhou Jiamo, Sheng Yihong, Sun Shenxing, Zhong Yuzheng, Yu Maoheng, and Cao Yubian, all devoted to the state and public service, white-haired elders of the highest stature.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the highest stature still remain—Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Wang Ji, Zhou Jiamo, Sheng Yihong, Sun Shenxing, Zhong Yuzheng, Yu Maoheng, Cao Yubian, and others—all white-haired elders who have served the state with devotion.

sentences.zh: 其他詞林臺諫一錮不起者，並皇國禎祥，盛朝珍寶。

translations.literal: Others among the literary academy and remonstrance offices who have been locked away and not raised up are likewise auspicious signs of the imperial realm and treasures of a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: Others in the Hanlin Academy and remonstrance offices who remain locked away are likewise treasures of a flourishing age and auspicious signs for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣不能汲致明廷，徒獻符貢瑞，臣竊羞之。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot draw them up to the bright court and would be ashamed merely to offer talismans and tribute omens.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot draw such men to court, and I would be ashamed merely to offer talismans and auspicious objects.

sentences.zh: 願陛下惟賢是寶。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would treasure only the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to treasure worthies above all.

sentences.zh: 在朝之忠直，勿事虛拘；

translations.literal: Let loyal and upright men at court not be held in empty constraint;
translations.idiomatic: Do not keep loyal and upright men at court in empty constraint;

sentences.zh: 在野之老成，亟圖登進。

translations.literal: and let seasoned elders in retirement be urgently brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: and urgently advance seasoned elders still in retirement.

sentences.zh: 彼區區秦璽之真偽，又安足計哉。」

translations.literal: As for the truth or falsehood of that petty Qin seal, how can it be worth considering?
translations.idiomatic: As for whether this petty Qin seal is genuine, what does it matter?

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢方斥逐耆碩，見之不悅。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian was then driving out elder statesmen and was displeased on reading this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was then driving out elder statesmen and took offense at the memorial.

sentences.zh: 後忠賢勢益張，紹遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Later, as Zhongxian's power grew still greater, Shao pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhongxian's power grew, Shao pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年，薦起工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was recommended and raised as right vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was recommended and appointed right vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 越二年，以年老，四疏乞休去。

translations.literal: Two years later, on account of old age, he submitted four memorials asking to retire and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, citing old age, he submitted four memorials requesting retirement and left office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the rank of minister of his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the rank of minister of his ministry.

sentences.zh: 翟鳳翀，字淩元，益都人。

translations.literal: Zhai Fengchong, styled Lingyuan, was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Fengchong, whose style was Lingyuan, came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知吳橋、任丘，有治聲，征授御史。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Wuqiao and Renqiu, gained a reputation for good administration, and was summoned as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Wuqiao and Renqiu with a reputation for good governance and was summoned as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 疏薦鐘羽正、趙南星、鄒元標等，因言：「宋季邪諂之徒，終日請禁偽學，信口詆諆。

translations.literal: In a memorial he recommended Zhong Yuzheng, Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, and others, saying: "The flatterers of the late Song spent all day asking to ban heterodox learning and slandered at will.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized recommending Zhong Yuzheng, Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, and others, writing: "The flatterers of late Song spent their days demanding bans on heterodox learning and slandering at will.

sentences.zh: 近年號講學者，不幸類此。」

translations.literal: Those in recent years who call themselves students of learning are, alas, of this same kind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who call themselves advocates of learning in recent years are, alas, much the same.

sentences.zh: 出按遼東。

translations.literal: He went out to tour Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to tour Liaodong as censor.

sentences.zh: 宰賽、暖兔二十四營環開原而居，歲為邊患。

translations.literal: The twenty-four camps of Zaisai and Nuan Tu encircled Kaiyuan and were a yearly frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four camps of Zaisai and Nuan Tu ringed Kaiyuan and plagued the frontier year after year.

sentences.zh: 宰賽尤桀驁，數敗官軍，殺守將，因挾邊吏增賞。

translations.literal: Zaisai was especially arrogant and fierce, repeatedly defeating government troops and killing defending generals, and thereby coerced frontier officials into increasing rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisai was especially arrogant, repeatedly defeating government troops and killing frontier commanders, then coercing officials into increasing rewards.

sentences.zh: 慶雲參將陳洪範所統止羸卒二千，又恇怯不任戰。

translations.literal: Chen Hongfan, regional commander of Qingyun, commanded only two thousand weak troops and was moreover timid and unfit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Chen Hongfan of Qingyun commanded only two thousand weak troops and was too timid for battle.

sentences.zh: 鳳翀奏請益兵，易置健將，開原始有備。

translations.literal: Fengchong memorialized asking for more troops, replacement with able generals, and that Kaiyuan originally had adequate defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchong memorialized for reinforcements, replacement of the commander with a capable general, and restoration of Kaiyuan's former defenses.

sentences.zh: 又請所在建常平倉，括贖鍰，節公費，易粟備荒。

translations.literal: He also asked that ever-normal granaries be built everywhere, fines be collected, public expenses be economized, and grain be exchanged to prepare against famine.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that ever-normal granaries be built everywhere, fines collected, public expenses cut, and grain stockpiled against famine.

sentences.zh: 帝善其議，命推行於諸邊。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposals and ordered them carried out on all frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposals and ordered them implemented on all frontiers.

sentences.zh: 故遼陽參將吳希漢失律聽勘，以內援二十年不決，且謀復官，鳳翀一訊成獄，置之大辟，邊人快之。

translations.literal: The former regional commander of Liaoyang Wu Xihan had violated discipline and was awaiting investigation; through inner connections the case went undecided for twenty years, and he even plotted to recover office; Fengchong completed the case in one inquiry, sentenced him to death, and the frontier people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Former Regional Commander Wu Xihan of Liaoyang had violated discipline and awaited trial; through court connections the case dragged on twenty years while he plotted reinstatement; Fengchong concluded the case in one hearing, sentenced him to death, and frontier people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 帝因「梃擊」之變，召見廷臣於慈寧宮。

translations.literal: Because of the "Club Assault" incident, the emperor summoned court officials for audience at the Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the Club Assault incident, the emperor summoned court officials to audience at the Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 大學士方從哲、吳道南無所言，御史劉光復方發口，遽得罪。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries Fang Congzhe and Wu Daonan had nothing to say; the censor Liu Guangfu had barely opened his mouth when he immediately offended and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Fang Congzhe and Wu Daonan said nothing; Censor Liu Guangfu had barely spoken when he was punished.

sentences.zh: 鳳翀上言：「陛下召對廷臣，天威開霽，千載一時。

translations.literal: Fengchong submitted: "When Your Majesty summoned court officials for audience, imperial majesty cleared like the sky—a moment once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchong wrote: "When Your Majesty summoned the court for audience, imperial majesty cleared like the sky—a moment that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 輔臣宜舉朝端大政，如皇太子、皇長孫講學，福府莊田鹺引，大僚空虛，考選沈閣，以及中旨頻降，邊警時聞，水旱盜賊之相仍，流移饑殍之載道，一一縷奏於前，乃緘默不言，致光復以失儀獲罪。

translations.literal: The chief ministers ought to have set forth the great policies of the court, such as instruction for the crown prince and imperial great-grandson, the manor lands and salt monopolies of the Fu princedom, the emptiness of high offices, the stagnation of examinations and selections, as well as frequent inner rescripts, frontier alarms heard from time to time, floods, droughts, and bandits succeeding one another, and displaced refugees and famine corpses filling the roads—item by item before the throne; instead they kept silent, causing Guangfu to be punished for breach of decorum.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers should have laid out the great affairs of state—the education of the crown prince and imperial great-grandson, the Fu princedom's manor lands and salt monopolies, empty high offices, stalled examinations and appointments, frequent inner rescripts, frontier alarms, successive floods, droughts, and banditry, and refugees and famine corpses filling the roads—item by item; instead they kept silent, leaving Guangfu punished for a breach of decorum.

sentences.zh: 光復一日未釋，輔臣未可晏然也。」

translations.literal: As long as Guangfu is not released for a single day, the chief ministers cannot be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As long as Guangfu remains unreleased, the chief ministers cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: The memorial offended the throne and he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial offended the throne and drew a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 山東大饑，以鳳翀疏，遣御史過庭訓賫十六萬金振之。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered great famine; on account of Fengchong's memorial, the censor Guo Tingxun was sent with one hundred sixty thousand taels of gold for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered great famine, the court sent Censor Guo Tingxun with one hundred sixty thousand taels of silver for relief on the strength of Fengchong's memorial.

sentences.zh: 中官呂貴假奸民奏，留督浙江織造。

translations.literal: The eunuch Lu Gui, on a false petition by a scoundrel, remained to supervise weaving in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Lu Gui, on a scoundrel's false petition, remained in Zhejiang to supervise imperial weaving.

sentences.zh: 冉登提督九門，誣奏市民毆門卒，下兵馬指揮歐相之吏。

translations.literal: Ran Deng, superintendent of the Nine Gates, falsely memorialized that citizens had beaten gate guards and had the cavalry command Ou Xiang's subordinates handed over to the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Deng, superintendent of the Nine Gates, falsely reported that citizens had beaten gate guards and had the cavalry commander's subordinates handed over to the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 邢洪辱御史淩漢翀於朝，給事中郭尚賓等劾之，帝釋洪不問。

translations.literal: Xing Hong insulted the censor Ling Hanchong at court; the supervising secretaries Guo Shangbin and others impeached him, but the emperor released Hong without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Hong insulted Censor Ling Hanchong at court; Supervising Secretary Guo Shangbin and others impeached him, but the emperor let him go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 漢翀為廢將淩應登所毆，洪復曲庇應登。

translations.literal: Hanchong had been beaten by the dismissed general Ling Yingdeng, and Hong again bent the law to protect Yingdeng.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchong had been beaten by the dismissed general Ling Yingdeng, and Hong again shielded Yingdeng.

sentences.zh: 鳳翀抗疏極論貴、登、洪三人罪，且曰：「大臣造膝無從，小臣叩閽無路。

translations.literal: Fengchong submitted a forceful memorial arguing at length the crimes of Gui, Deng, and Hong, saying moreover: "Great ministers have no access for intimate counsel, and lesser officials have no way to knock at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchong submitted a forceful memorial detailing the crimes of Gui, Deng, and Hong, writing: "Great ministers have no access for intimate counsel, and lesser officials have no way to reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 宦寺浸用，政令多違，實開群小假借之端，成太阿倒持之勢。」

translations.literal: Eunuchs are increasingly employed, government orders are often violated, and this truly opens the way for petty men to borrow authority and creates the situation of holding the sword by the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs are increasingly employed, edicts are often ignored, and this opens the way for petty men to borrow authority—creating a situation in which power is held by the blade rather than the hilt.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謫山西按察使經歷。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and banished him to assistant surveillance commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted him to assistant surveillance commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 而是時，尚賓亦上疏極言：「比來擬旨不由內閣，托以親裁。

translations.literal: At this time Shangbin also submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Recently draft rescripts have not come from the Grand Secretariat but have been entrusted to personal decision.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Shangbin submitted a forceful memorial: "Recently draft rescripts have bypassed the Grand Secretariat under the label of personal imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 言官稍涉同類，輒雲黨附，將使大臣不肯盡言，小臣不敢抗論，天下事尚可為哉？

translations.literal: If remonstrance officials touch even slightly on like-minded association, they are at once said to be clique followers; this will make great ministers unwilling to speak fully and lesser officials afraid to argue in opposition—can affairs under Heaven still be managed?
translations.idiomatic: If remonstrance officials are even slightly associated with like-minded colleagues, they are accused of factionalism; great ministers will refuse to speak fully and lesser officials will fear to argue—can the empire still be governed?

sentences.zh: 乞陛下明詔閣臣，封還內降，容納直諫，以保治安。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict to the Grand Secretariat to seal and return inner rescripts, accept forthright remonstrance, and thereby preserve peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict requiring the Grand Secretariat to seal and return inner rescripts, accept forthright remonstrance, and preserve peace and order.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，謫江西布政使檢校。

translations.literal: The memorial offended the throne and he was banished to inspector of the Jiangxi provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial offended the throne and he was demoted to inspector of the Jiangxi provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 閣臣及言官論救，皆不納。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries and remonstrance officials pleaded for their rescue, but none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries and remonstrance officials pleaded for them, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 帝於章疏多不省，故廷臣直諫者久不被譴。

translations.literal: The emperor often did not read through memorials, so court officials who remonstrated forthrightly had long gone unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor often did not read memorials through, forthright remonstrators had long escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 至是二人同日謫官，時稱「二諫」。

translations.literal: On this occasion the two men were banished from office on the same day, and they were called at the time "the two remonstrators."
translations.idiomatic: When the two men were demoted on the same day, contemporaries called them "the two remonstrators."

sentences.zh: 鳳翀既謫，三遷。

translations.literal: After Fengchong had been demoted, he was transferred three times.
translations.idiomatic: Once demoted, Fengchong was reassigned three times.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，為南京光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he served as vice minister of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he became vice minister of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 四年，以大理少卿進右僉都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he advanced from vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review to right vice censor-in-chief and became grand coordinator of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was promoted from vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review to right vice censor-in-chief and sent to govern Yan-sui as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢黨御史卓邁、汪若極連章論之，遂削籍。

translations.literal: Censors Zhuo Mai and Wang Ruoji, partisans of Wei Zhongxian, memorialized against him in succession, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhuo Mai and Wang Ruoji, allies of Wei Zhongxian, attacked him in a series of memorials, and he was stripped from office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起兵部右侍郎，尋出撫天津。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled as right vice minister of War and soon went out to grand coordinate Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year two he was made right vice minister of War and soon sent out to govern Tianjin as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尚賓，字朝諤，南海人，鳳翀同年進士。

translations.literal: Shangbin, styled Chaoe, was a native of Nanhai and a jinshi in the same year as Fengchong.
translations.idiomatic: Shangbin, styled Chaoe, was from Nanhai and had passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Fengchong.

sentences.zh: 自吉安推官授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: From the post of magistrate's aide at Ji'an he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate's aide at Ji'an to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 遇事輒諫諍，尤憤中官之橫。

translations.literal: When matters arose he would remonstrate forthwith, especially resenting the overbearing ways of eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated at every turn and particularly hated eunuch arrogance.

sentences.zh: 嘗因事論稅使李鳳、高寀、潘相，頗稱敢言。

translations.literal: Once, on a matter at hand, he criticized the tax commissioners Li Feng, Gao Cai, and Pan Xiang and was widely praised for daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he criticized the tax commissioners Li Feng, Gao Cai, and Pan Xiang and gained a reputation for bold speech.

sentences.zh: 已，竟謫官。

translations.literal: In the end he was demoted from office.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was banished from office.

sentences.zh: 光宗時乃復起，累官刑部右侍郎，亦以不附忠賢削籍。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Guangzong he was raised again and rose to right vice minister of Justice, but likewise because he would not follow Zhongxian was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored under Guangzong and eventually reached right vice minister of Justice, but was again struck from the rolls for refusing to align with Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he served as right vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he became right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of minister.

sentences.zh: 洪文衡，字平仲，歙人。

translations.literal: Hong Wenheng, styled Pingzhong, was a native of She.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Wenheng, styled Pingzhong, was from She.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year seventeen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝將封皇長子為王，偕同官賈巖合疏爭。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to enfeoff the eldest imperial son as a prince, he joined his colleague Jia Yan in a joint memorial protesting.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to enfeoff the eldest imperial son as a prince, he and his colleague Jia Yan submitted a joint memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮部。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 與郎中何喬遠善，喬遠坐詿誤被謫，文衡已遷考功主事，竟引病歸。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the bureau director He Qiaoyuan; when Qiaoyuan was demoted on a charge of error, Wenheng had already been moved to director in the Bureau of Merit, yet in the end he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to bureau director He Qiaoyuan; when Qiaoyuan was demoted on a procedural charge, Wenheng had already been promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, but he still cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 起補南京工部，歷郎中。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was placed in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and rose through the directorships.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the Nanjing Ministry of Works, he served through successive bureau directorships.

sentences.zh: 力按舊章，杜中貴橫索，節冗費為多。

translations.literal: He enforced the old regulations strenuously, blocked eunuchs' arbitrary demands, and saved much superfluous expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced old regulations rigorously, blocked eunuchs' arbitrary exactions, and cut a great deal of wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 官工部九年，進光祿少卿。

translations.literal: After nine years in the Works ministry he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in the Ministry of Works he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 改太常，督四夷館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Court of Sacrificial Worship and supervised the Bureau for Tribute from the Four Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Court of Sacrificial Worship and put in charge of the Bureau for Tribute from the Four Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 中外競請起廢，帝率報寢。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court all competed to ask for recall of the dismissed, but the emperor consistently replied that the matter was tabled.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inside and outside the court clamored for dismissed men to be recalled, but the emperor routinely shelved the requests.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃特起顧憲成。

translations.literal: After a long time he specially recalled Gu Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay did he specially recall Gu Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 憲成已辭疾，忌者猶憚其進用，御史徐兆魁首疏力攻之。

translations.literal: Xiancheng had already declined on grounds of illness, yet those who envied him still feared his appointment; Censor Xu Zhaokui was first with a memorial vehemently attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had already declined on grounds of illness, yet his enemies still feared his appointment; Censor Xu Zhaokui led the attack with a vehement memorial.

sentences.zh: 文衡慮帝惑兆魁言，抗章申雪，因言：「今兩都九列，強半無人，仁賢空虛，識者浩嘆。

translations.literal: Wenheng feared the emperor would be misled by Zhaokui's words and submitted a forceful memorial to vindicate him, saying: "Today among the nine ranks of both capitals, more than half are unfilled; worthies stand vacant, and those who see sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng feared the emperor would be swayed by Zhaokui and submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, writing: "Today more than half the senior posts in both capitals stand empty; the ranks of the worthy are hollow, and informed observers sigh in despair.

sentences.zh: 所堪選擇而使者，只此起廢一途。

translations.literal: The path that may still be chosen for appointment is only this one of recalling the dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The only avenue left for choosing and appointing men is this path of recalling the dismissed.

sentences.zh: 今憲成尚在田間，已嬰羅罔，俾聖心愈疑。

translations.literal: Now Xiancheng is still in the countryside yet already caught in a net, making the sacred heart all the more doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng is still in retirement yet already entangled in accusations, which can only deepen Your Majesty's doubts.

sentences.zh: 連茹無望，貽禍賢者，流毒國家，實兆魁一疏塞之矣。」

translations.literal: There is no hope of drawing worthy men together; harm to the worthy and poison to the state—truly Zhaokui's one memorial has blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: There is no hope of gathering worthy men in office; harm to the worthy and poison to the state—truly Xu Zhaokui's single memorial has blocked the way.

sentences.zh: 尋進大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年起太常卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he was made minister of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang he was appointed minister of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.

sentences.zh: 光宗既崩，議升祔。

translations.literal: After Emperor Guangzong's death, the court debated raising his tablet for joint worship.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzong's death, the court debated installing his spirit tablet for joint worship.

sentences.zh: 文衡請祧睿宗，曰：「此肅宗一時崇奉之情，不合古誼。

translations.literal: Wenheng asked to move out Ruizong's tablet, saying: "This was only the Jiajing emperor's momentary devotion and does not accord with ancient propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng petitioned to remove Ruizong's tablet, writing: "This was only the Jiajing emperor's momentary devotion and violates ancient ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 且睿宗嘗為武宗臣矣，一旦加諸其上，禮既不合，情亦未安。

translations.literal: Moreover Ruizong was once a subject of Wuzong; to place him suddenly above is improper in ritual and uneasy in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ruizong had once been a subject of Wuzong; to set him suddenly above Wuzong is ritually improper and emotionally unsettling.

sentences.zh: 當時臣子過於將順，因循至今。

translations.literal: Ministers of that time went too far in compliance, and the practice has dragged on to today.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of that day went too far in flattery, and the error has persisted to the present.

sentences.zh: 夫情隆於一時，禮垂於萬世，更定之舉正在今時。」

translations.literal: Feeling may flourish for a moment, but ritual endures for ten thousand generations—the work of revision is precisely for now.
translations.idiomatic: A moment's emotion may run high, but ritual endures for ten thousand generations; the work of correction must be done now.

sentences.zh: 疏格不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，贈工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as right vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died and was posthumously granted the title of right vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 文衡天性孝友。

translations.literal: Wenheng was by nature filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng was by nature devoted in filial piety and brotherly love.

sentences.zh: 居喪，斷酒肉不處內者三年。

translations.literal: During mourning he abstained from wine and meat and did not enter the inner quarters for three years.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning he abstained from wine and meat and did not enter the inner quarters for three years.

sentences.zh: 生平不妄取一介。

translations.literal: In his life he never took a single thing unrightfully.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he never accepted the smallest thing unrightfully.

sentences.zh: 喬遠，字稚孝，晉江人。

translations.literal: Qiaoyuan, styled Zhixiao, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoyuan, styled Zhixiao, was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year fourteen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，歷禮部儀制郎中。

translations.literal: He was made a director in the Ministry of Justice and served through as bureau director of Ritual Regulation in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice and later served as bureau director of Ritual Regulation in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 神宗欲封皇長子為王，喬遠力爭不可。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong wished to enfeoff the eldest imperial son as a prince, Qiaoyuan argued strenuously that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong sought to enfeoff the eldest imperial son as a prince, Qiaoyuan argued forcefully that it must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 同官陳泰來等言事被謫，抗疏救之。

translations.literal: His colleagues Chen Tailai and others were demoted for speaking on affairs; he submitted a forceful memorial to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When his colleagues Chen Tailai and others were demoted for remonstrating, he submitted a forceful memorial to save them.

sentences.zh: 石星主封倭，而朝鮮使臣金晬泣言李如松、沈惟敬之誤，致國人束手受刃者六萬余人。

translations.literal: Shi Xing advocated appeasing the Japanese, while the Korean envoy Jin Zui wept and said that through the errors of Li Rusong and Shen Weijing more than sixty thousand of their countrymen had been left helpless to receive the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xing favored appeasing Japan, but the Korean envoy Jin Zui tearfully reported that the mistakes of Li Rusong and Shen Weijing had left more than sixty thousand of his countrymen helpless before the sword.

sentences.zh: 喬遠即以聞，因進累朝馭倭故事，帝頗心動。

translations.literal: Qiaoyuan immediately reported it and presented precedents from successive reigns on controlling the Japanese; the emperor was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoyuan reported this at once and submitted precedents from successive reigns on controlling Japan; the emperor was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 而星堅持己說，疏竟不行。

translations.literal: But Xing held to his own view and the memorial in the end was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: But Shi Xing held to his own view, and the memorial was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 坐累謫廣西布政使經歷，以事歸。

translations.literal: On cumulative charges he was demoted to assistant in the Guangxi provincial administration commission and returned home on business.
translations.idiomatic: On cumulative charges he was demoted to assistant in the Guangxi provincial administration commission and returned home.

sentences.zh: 裏居二十余年，中外交薦，不起。

translations.literal: He lived at home more than twenty years; inside and outside the court all recommended him, but he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for more than twenty years; court and provinces alike recommended him, but he refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，召為光祿少卿，移太仆。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王化貞駐兵廣寧，主戰。

translations.literal: Wang Huazhen stationed troops at Guangning and favored war.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huazhen held troops at Guangning and advocated war.

sentences.zh: 喬遠畫守禦策，力言不宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Qiaoyuan drafted a defensive strategy and argued forcefully that rash action should not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoyuan drafted a defensive strategy and argued forcefully against rash military action.

sentences.zh: 無何，廣寧竟棄。

translations.literal: Before long Guangning was indeed abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guangning was indeed lost.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進左通政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to left chief administrator of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year two he was promoted to left chief administrator of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 鄒元標建首善書院，朱童蒙等劾之，喬遠言：「書院上梁文實出臣手，義當並罷。」

translations.literal: When Zou Yuanbiao built the Shoushan Academy, Zhu Tongmeng and others impeached it; Qiaoyuan said: "The academy's rafter inscription actually came from my hand; by right I should be dismissed together with it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Yuanbiao founded the Shoushan Academy, Zhu Tongmeng and others impeached it; Qiaoyuan wrote: "The academy's beam-raising inscription came from my own hand; by right I should be dismissed along with it.

sentences.zh: 語侵童蒙。

translations.literal: The words impinged on Tongmeng.
translations.idiomatic: His words were aimed at Tongmeng.

sentences.zh: 進光祿卿、通政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and chief administrator of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and chief administrator of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 五疏引疾，以戶部右侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: After five memorials citing illness he retired as right vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After five memorials citing illness he retired with the rank of right vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled as right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year two he was recalled as right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧兆龍劾其衰庸，自引去。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Lu Zhaolong impeached him as decrepit and incompetent, and he withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Lu Zhaolong impeached him as senile and incompetent, and he withdrew on his own initiative.

sentences.zh: 喬遠博覽，好著書。

translations.literal: Qiaoyuan was broadly learned and fond of writing books.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoyuan was widely read and fond of authorship.

sentences.zh: 嘗輯明十三朝遺事為《名山藏》，又纂《閩書》百五十卷，頗行於世，然援據多舛雲。

translations.literal: He once compiled surviving tales of the thirteen Ming reigns into 《Famous Mountains Store》, and also compiled 《Books of Min》 in 150 juan, which circulated widely in the world, yet its citations are often wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled surviving tales from the thirteen Ming reigns into 《Famous Mountains Store》, and also compiled 《Books of Min》 in 150 juan, which circulated widely, though its citations are often unreliable.

sentences.zh: 陳伯友，字仲恬，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Boyou, styled Zhongtian, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Boyou, styled Zhongtian, was from Jining.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year twenty-nine he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed a courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the courier service.

sentences.zh: 擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
