translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 甫拜命，即罷河南巡撫李思孝。

translations.literal: As soon as he received the appointment, he moved to dismiss Grand Coordinator Li Sixiao of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office, he memorialized to dismiss Grand Coordinator Li Sixiao of Henan.

sentences.zh: 俄論鄒之麟科場弊宜勘；

translations.literal: Soon he argued that the examination-field abuses of Zou Zhilin should be investigated;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he argued that examination abuses involving Zou Zhilin should be investigated;

sentences.zh: 奄豎辱駙馬冉興讓，宜置之法；

translations.literal: that when a eunuch insulted the imperial son-in-law Ran Xingrang, the law should be applied;
translations.idiomatic: that when a eunuch insulted the imperial son-in-law Ran Xingrang, the offender should be punished by law;

sentences.zh: 楚宗英憔、蘊鈁，良吏滿朝薦、王邦才等宜釋。

translations.literal: that Ying Qiao and Yun Qin of the Chu princely house, and good officials such as Man Chaochang and Wang Bangcai, ought to be released.
translations.idiomatic: that Ying Qiao and Yun Qin of the Chu princely house, and worthy officials such as Man Chaochang and Wang Bangcai, ought to be released.

sentences.zh: 已，又言：「陛下清明之心，不幸中年為利所惑，皇皇焉若不足，以致財匱民艱，家成徹骨之貧，人抱傷心之痛。

translations.literal: Then he also said: "Your Majesty's clear and bright heart, unfortunately in midlife has been beguiled by profit, restless as if never enough, until the treasury is drained, the people hard pressed, the state reduced to poverty to the bone, and men bear wounds in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote: "Your Majesty's clear mind has, in midlife, been beguiled by profit; restless as though never satisfied, until the treasury is empty, the people strained, the state reduced to bone-deep poverty, and the people left heartbroken.

sentences.zh: 今天下所以杌隉傾危而不可救藥者，此也。」

translations.literal: The reason the realm today is unsettled, tottering, and beyond remedy is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the realm today is unstable, tottering, and beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 又言：「李廷機去國，操縱不出上裁。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Li Tingji left office, control did not issue from imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "When Li Tingji left office, power was wielded without imperial sanction.

sentences.zh: 至外而撫按，內而庶僚，去留無所斷決。

translations.literal: Whether grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners outside or the myriad officials within, none had firm decision on departure or retention.
translations.idiomatic: Whether grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners in the provinces or the myriad officials at court, no one could secure a clear decision on who should stay or go.

sentences.zh: 士大夫意見分岐，議論各異，陛下漫無批答。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials' views diverged and their debates differed, yet Your Majesty gave no responses at random.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials were divided in opinion and debate, yet Your Majesty offered no clear responses.

sentences.zh: 曷若盡付外廷公議，於以平曲直、定國是乎？」

translations.literal: Why not hand all entirely to public deliberation in the outer court, thereby to settle right and wrong and fix the nation's course?
translations.idiomatic: Why not leave everything to open deliberation in the outer court, so that right and wrong may be settled and the nation's course fixed?

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took note of none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it all.

sentences.zh: 熊廷弼為荊養喬所訐，伯友與李成名等力主行勘。

translations.literal: When Xiong Tingbi was impeached by Jing Yangqiao, Boyou and Li Chengming and others strongly urged that an investigation be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tingbi was impeached by Jing Yangqiao, Boyou joined Li Chengming and others in strongly urging a formal investigation.

sentences.zh: 既又陳時政四事，言：「擬旨必由內閣。

translations.literal: He then also set forth four points on current policy, saying: "Draft rescripts must pass through the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth four points on current affairs, writing: "Draft rescripts must pass through the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昨科臣曾六德之處分，閣臣葉向高之典試，悉由內降。

translations.literal: Yesterday's disposition of the censor Zeng Liude and Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao's presiding over the examinations all came by inner rescript.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's punishment of censor Zeng Liude and Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao's appointment to preside over the examinations both came by inner rescript.

sentences.zh: 而福王之國之旨，亦於他疏批行。

translations.literal: Yet the edict on the Prince of Fu taking up his fief was also approved on another memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edict on the Prince of Fu's departure to his fief was also approved on another memorial.

sentences.zh: 非獨褻天言，抑且貽陰禍。

translations.literal: This not only profanes heavenly words but also invites hidden calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This not only profanes imperial words but also invites hidden calamity.

sentences.zh: 法者天下所共，黔國公沐昌祚請令其孫啟元代鎮，已非法矣。

translations.literal: Law is what the realm shares in common; the Duke of Qian Mu Changzuo asked that his grandson Qiyuan hold the commandery in his stead, which was already unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Law belongs to the whole realm; the Duke of Qian, Mu Changzuo, asked that his grandson Qiyuan hold the commandery in his stead, which was already unlawful.

sentences.zh: 乃撫按據法請勘，而以內批免之，疑中有隱情。

translations.literal: Yet when grand coordinators and commissioners asked for investigation according to law, an inner rescript exempted him—raising suspicion of hidden circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when provincial officials asked for investigation under the law, an inner rescript exempted him, raising suspicion of hidden dealings.

sentences.zh: 御史呂圖南改提學，此爭為賢，彼爭為不肖，盍息兩家戈矛，共圖軍國大計？

translations.literal: When Censor Lü Tunan was changed to education intendant, one side fought that he was worthy and the other that he was unworthy—why not lay down both sides' spears and together plan the great affairs of army and state?
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Lü Tunan was reassigned as education intendant, one faction praised him as worthy and another denounced him as unworthy—why not lay down both factions' quarrels and together address the great affairs of army and state?

sentences.zh: 福王久應之國，今春催請不下數百疏，何以忽易期？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu long should have gone to his fief; this spring hundreds of memorials urging it were not answered—why suddenly change the deadline?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu should long since have gone to his fief; this spring hundreds of memorials urging departure went unanswered—why suddenly change the deadline?

sentences.zh: 疏亦留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was also kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: That memorial, too, was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 尋以艱去。

translations.literal: Soon he left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 及服除，廷議多排東林，遂不出。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, court discussion largely excluded the Donglin faction, and he therefore did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, court opinion largely excluded the Donglin faction, and he therefore did not return to office.

sentences.zh: 至四十六年，以年例，即家除河南副使。

translations.literal: By the forty-sixth year, under the routine of annual promotion, he was appointed from home as vice commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, under the routine of annual promotion, he was appointed from home as vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，屢遷太常寺卿，治少卿事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Court of Sacrificial Worship, administering the vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year four he was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Court of Sacrificial Worship, while performing the duties of the vice minister.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾魏忠賢，伯友亦偕卿胡世賞等抗疏極論。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Boyou also joined Minister Hu Shishang and others in a forceful memorial arguing at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Boyou joined Minister Hu Shishang and others in a forceful memorial denouncing him at length.

sentences.zh: 明年十二月，御史張樞劾其倚附東林，遂削奪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the next year Censor Zhang Shu impeached him for leaning on the Donglin faction, and he was struck and deprived.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year Censor Zhang Shu impeached him for relying on the Donglin faction, and he was stripped of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，詔復官，未及用而卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded, an edict restored his office, but before he could be employed he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen emperor took the throne, an edict restored his office, but he died before he could be appointed.

sentences.zh: 成名，字寰知，太原衛人。

translations.literal: Li Chengming, styled Huanzhi, was a man of Taiyuan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengming, whose courtesy name was Huanzhi, came from Taiyuan Guard.

sentences.zh: 祖應時，南京戶部員外郎，以清白著。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ying Shi was an assistant department director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, renowned for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ying Shi had served as an assistant department director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and was famed for his spotless conduct.

sentences.zh: 成名舉萬歷三十二年進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: Chengming passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli and was appointed a Secretariat draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Chengming earned his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign and was made a draftsman in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏陳銓政失平，語侵尚書趙煥。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that appointment policy was unbalanced, with wording that impugned Minister Zhao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that personnel appointments had grown unfair, and his language impugned Minister Zhao Huan.

sentences.zh: 俄請釋累臣滿朝薦，言朝薦不釋則諸珰日肆，國家患無已。

translations.literal: Soon he petitioned to release the burdened official Man Chaojian, saying that if Chaojian were not released the eunuchs would grow more reckless day by day and the state's troubles would never end.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned for the release of Man Chaojian, a long-imprisoned official, arguing that unless Chaojian were freed the eunuchs would grow bolder each day and the dynasty's troubles would never cease.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎方從哲，中旨起官，成名抗疏劾之，並及其子恣橫狀。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Congzhe was reappointed by an edict delivered outside normal channels, Chengming submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him and also describing the wanton conduct of his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Congzhe, vice minister of personnel, was recalled to office by an irregular palace edict, Chengming submitted a bold memorial impeaching him and detailing the lawless behavior of his son.

sentences.zh: 從哲求去，帝不許。

translations.literal: Congzhe asked to resign; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe asked to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，黨人日攻東林，成名遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: At that time factionalists daily attacked the Donglin faction, and Chengming thereupon cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Factionalists were then assailing the Donglin party day after day, and Chengming cited illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 家居五年，起山東副使。

translations.literal: After five years at home he was recalled as deputy commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in retirement he was recalled as deputy commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，遷湖廣參政，入為太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was transferred to administrative commissioner of Huguang, then entered the capital as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was moved to administrative commissioner of Huguang, then brought into the capital as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 四年春，擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢以成名為趙南星所用，因所屬給由，犯禦諱，除其名。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian, because Chengming had been employed by Zhao Nanxing, took the credentials submitted on his behalf, found them to violate a taboo on the imperial name, and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian, regarding Chengming as a man Zhao Nanxing had used, seized the credentials his subordinates had submitted, found a violation of the imperial name taboo, and struck his name from office.

sentences.zh: 為巡撫止八月，士民祠祀焉。

translations.literal: He served as grand coordinator only eight months, yet officials and commoners erected temples to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served as grand coordinator only eight months, officials and commoners erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，召拜戶部右侍郎，以左侍郎專理邊餉。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen era began he was summoned and appointed right vice minister of Revenue, and as left vice minister he specialized in frontier provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen reign began he was summoned as right vice minister of Revenue and, as left vice minister, placed in charge of frontier supplies.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，改兵部。

translations.literal: When the capital was placed under martial law, he was moved to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was placed under martial law, he was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 帝召對平臺，區畫兵事甚悉。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience at the terrace and he laid out military affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to audience on the terrace, and he mapped out military affairs with meticulous thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 數月而罷，卒於家。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was dismissed and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was dismissed from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 董應舉，字崇相，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Yingju, styled Chongxiang, was a man of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yingju, whose courtesy name was Chongxiang, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除廣州教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed professor at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 與稅監李鳳爭學傍壖地，鳳舍人馳騎文廟前，縶其馬，用是有名。

translations.literal: He disputed with the tax commissioner Li Feng over land beside the academy embankment; Feng's household attendant galloped his horse before the Confucian temple, and Yingju seized the horse, whereby he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with the tax commissioner Li Feng over land beside the school embankment; when Feng's retainer galloped through the ground before the Confucian temple, Yingju seized his horse—and thereby won renown.

sentences.zh: 遷南京國子博士，再遷南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to doctorate of the Nanjing Imperial Academy, then again to a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to a doctorate at the Nanjing Imperial Academy, then again to a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 召為文選主事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be a clerk in the Selection Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a clerk in the Selection Office.

sentences.zh: 歷考功郎中，告歸。

translations.literal: After serving as director in the Ministry of Personnel's Records Office, he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a director in the Records Office, he petitioned to retire and went home.

sentences.zh: 起南京大理丞。

translations.literal: He was recalled as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 四十六年閏四月，日中黑子相鬥。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the forty-sixth year, black spots on the sun grappled with one another at midday.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of the forty-sixth year, black sunspots seemed to wrestle with one another at noon.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，有黑日掩日，日無光。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, a black sun covered the sun and the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month a black disk blotted out the sun until it shone no more.

sentences.zh: 時遼東撫順已失，應舉言：「日生黑眚，乃強敵侵淩之征。

translations.literal: At that time Fushun in Liaodong had already fallen. Yingju said: "When the sun produces a black calamity, it is a sign of a powerful enemy's encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Fushun in Liaodong had already fallen. Yingju said, "When the sun shows a black omen, it is a sign that a powerful foe is pressing upon us.

sentences.zh: 亟宜勤政修備，以消禍變。」

translations.literal: We should urgently attend to government and strengthen defenses to dispel this omen.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should urgently attend to government and strengthen defenses to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 因條上方略。

translations.literal: He then itemized strategies above.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out a series of strategic proposals.

sentences.zh: 帝置不省。

translations.literal: The emperor set it aside and took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set the memorial aside and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 天啟改元，再遷太常少卿，督四夷館。

translations.literal: When the Tianqi reign began he was again promoted to vice minister of Rites and supervised the Four Barbarians Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianqi reign began he was promoted again to vice minister of Rites and put in charge of the Four Barbarians Institute.

sentences.zh: 二年春，陳急務數事，極言天下兵耗民離，疆宇日蹙，由主威不立，國法不行所致。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he presented several urgent matters, stating emphatically that troops were exhausted, the people scattered, and territory daily shrinking—all because sovereign authority was not established and state law was not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he laid out several urgent matters, arguing forcefully that armies were exhausted, the people estranged, and the realm shrinking day by day—all because the throne's authority stood unsteady and the laws of the state went unenforced.

sentences.zh: 帝以為應舉知兵，令專任較射演武。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Yingju understood warfare and ordered him to specialize in archery competitions and military drills.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Yingju understood military affairs and put him solely in charge of archery trials and martial drills.

sentences.zh: 已，上言保衛神京在設險營屯。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized that defending the sacred capital depended on establishing fortified garrison colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized that the defense of the sacred capital lay in establishing fortified garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 遂擢應舉太仆卿兼河南道御史，經理天津至山海屯務。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and concurrently censor of the Henan circuit, to manage garrison-colony affairs from Tianjin to Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and concurrently made censor of the Henan circuit, charged with managing garrison colonies from Tianjin to Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 應舉以責太重，陳十難十利，帝悉敕所司從之。

translations.literal: Yingju, finding the responsibility too heavy, presented ten difficulties and ten advantages; the emperor ordered all relevant offices to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the burden too great, Yingju set forth ten difficulties and ten advantages; the emperor ordered every relevant office to follow his plan.

sentences.zh: 乃分處遼人萬三千余戶於順天、永平、河間、保定，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: He then distributed more than thirteen thousand households of Liaodong people across Shuntian, Yongping, Hejian, and Baoding; an imperial edict praised the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled more than thirteen thousand Liaodong households across Shuntian, Yongping, Hejian, and Baoding, and an imperial edict commended the work.

sentences.zh: 遂用公帑六千買民田十二萬余畝，合閑田凡十八萬畝，廣募耕者，畀工廩、田器、牛種，浚渠築防，教之藝稻，農舍、倉廨、場圃、舟車畢具，費二萬六千，而所收黍麥谷五萬五千余石。

translations.literal: He then used six thousand taels of public funds to buy more than 120,000 mu of private fields; together with idle land the total reached 180,000 mu. He widely recruited cultivators, supplied labor rations, farm tools, and seed oxen, dredged canals and built dikes, taught them to plant rice, and fully equipped farmhouses, granaries, threshing yards, boats, and carts—at a cost of 26,000, yet harvesting more than 55,000 shi of millet, wheat, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He spent six thousand taels from the public treasury to buy more than 120,000 mu of private land; with idle fields added, the total reached 180,000 mu. He recruited cultivators on a broad scale, furnished labor rations, farm tools, and oxen for seeding, dredged canals and built dikes, and taught them to grow rice. Farmhouses, granaries, threshing yards, boats, and carts were all provided at a cost of 26,000 taels, yet the harvest yielded more than 55,000 shi of millet, wheat, and grain.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多論其功，就進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Many court officials commended his achievements and he was promptly promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials widely praised his achievements, and he was promptly promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天津葛沽故有水陸兵二千，應舉奏令屯田，以所入充歲餉，屯利益興。

translations.literal: At Gegu in Tianjin there had been two thousand land and naval troops; Yingju memorialized that they should farm colony land, using the proceeds to cover annual provisions, and garrison-colony profits flourished.
translations.idiomatic: At Gegu in Tianjin there had formerly been two thousand land and naval troops; Yingju memorialized that they should farm garrison land, using the yield to meet annual provisions, and the profits of the colonies began to rise.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，朝議以屯務既成，當廣鼓鑄。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year the court discussed that with the colony work complete, coinage should be expanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year the court debated that, with the garrison colonies established, coinage ought to be expanded.

sentences.zh: 乃改應舉工部右侍郎，專領錢務，開局荊州。

translations.literal: Yingju was therefore changed to right vice minister of Works, charged solely with coinage, and opened a mint at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju was therefore transferred to right vice minister of Works, placed solely in charge of coinage, and opened a mint at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋議給兩淮鹽課為鑄本，命兼戶部侍郎，並理鹽政。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided to allocate the salt tax of the two Huai circuits as casting capital; he was ordered to serve concurrently as vice minister of Revenue and jointly administer salt policy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court resolved to supply the salt revenues of the two Huai circuits as casting capital, and ordered him to serve concurrently as vice minister of Revenue while also overseeing salt administration.

sentences.zh: 應舉至揚州，疏請厘正鹽規，議商人補行積引，增輸銀視正引之半，為部議所格。

translations.literal: When Yingju reached Yangzhou he memorialized to rectify salt regulations, proposing that merchants make up accumulated salt certificates and pay additional silver at half the rate of standard certificates; the ministry's deliberation blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingju reached Yangzhou he memorialized to reform the salt regulations, proposing that merchants redeem accumulated salt certificates and pay supplemental silver at half the rate of a standard certificate—but the ministry's deliberation blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 應舉方奏析，而巡鹽御史陸世科惡其侵官，劾之，魏忠賢傳旨詰讓，御史徐揚先遂希指再劾，落職閑住。

translations.literal: While Yingju was still memorializing in analysis, the salt-inspecting censor Lu Shike, resenting his encroachment on authority, impeached him; Wei Zhongxian transmitted an edict of rebuke; censor Xu Yangxian then, toadying to the intent, impeached him again, and he was stripped of office to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingju was still submitting explanatory memorials, the touring salt censor Lu Shike, resenting his encroachment on another's jurisdiction, impeached him. Wei Zhongxian transmitted an edict of rebuke, and the censor Xu Yangxian, eager to follow the cue, impeached him again. Yingju was dismissed and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 應舉好學善文。

translations.literal: Yingju loved learning and was skilled in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju loved learning and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 其居官，慷慨任事；

translations.literal: In office he was magnanimous and undertook affairs boldly;
translations.idiomatic: In office he was openhanded and bold in undertaking affairs;

sentences.zh: 在家，好興利捍患。

translations.literal: at home he liked to promote profit and repel harm.
translations.idiomatic: at home he delighted in promoting public benefit and warding off calamity.

sentences.zh: 比沒，海濱人祠祀之。

translations.literal: After his death, people along the seacoast enshrined and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, people along the coast erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 林材，字謹任，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Lin Cai, styled Jinren, was a man of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Cai, whose courtesy name was Jinren, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授舒城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 吏部推鄭洛戎政尚書，起張九一貴州巡撫，材極言兩人不當用，九一遂罷。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel recommended Zheng Luo as minister of frontier military affairs and recalled Zhang Jiuyi as grand coordinator of Guizhou. Cai spoke forcefully that neither man should be used, and Jiuyi's appointment was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel recommended Zheng Luo for minister of frontier military affairs and recalled Zhang Jiuyi as grand coordinator of Guizhou, Cai argued vehemently that neither appointment was fit—and Jiuyi's recall was dropped.

sentences.zh: 王錫爵赴召，材疏論，並及趙誌臯、張位。

translations.literal: When Wang Xijue answered the summons, Cai memorialized in criticism, also implicating Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xijue answered the imperial summons, Cai memorialized against him and also took Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei to task.

sentences.zh: 再請建儲豫教，又爭三王並封之謬。

translations.literal: He again petitioned to establish the heir apparent and provide him early instruction, and again contested the error of enfeoffing the three princes together.
translations.idiomatic: He again petitioned to invest the crown prince and provide him early instruction, and again fought the folly of enfeoffing all three princes at once.

sentences.zh: 屢遷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: After repeated transfers he became chief supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became chief supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 劾罷南京尚書郝傑、徐元泰。

translations.literal: He impeached and brought about the dismissal of the Nanjing ministers Hao Jie and Xu Yuantai.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and brought down the Nanjing ministers Hao Jie and Xu Yuantai.

sentences.zh: 經略宋應昌惑沈惟敬，力請封貢，材乞斬應昌、惟敬，不報。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Song Yingchang was deluded by Shen Weijing and strongly petitioned for investiture and tribute; Cai begged that Yingchang and Weijing be executed, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissioner Song Yingchang had been misled by Shen Weijing and pressed hard for enfeoffment and tribute payments. Cai petitioned that both men be executed, but the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 誌臯、位擬旨失當，材抗疏駁之。

translations.literal: Zhigao and Wei drafted edicts improperly; Cai submitted a forceful memorial to refute them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao and Wei drafted edicts improperly, Cai submitted a bold memorial refuting them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏六月，西華門災，材偕同官上言，切指時政缺失。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the twenty-second year the Xihua Gate burned; Cai together with his colleagues submitted a memorial, sharply pointing to deficiencies in current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the twenty-second year fire struck the Xihua Gate; Cai and his colleagues memorialized together, pointing sharply to failings in current governance.

sentences.zh: 帝慍甚，以方修省不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered but, because he was then practicing self-restraint, did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply angered, yet because he was then observing a period of self-restraint he imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 吏部推顧養謹總理河道，材論止之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel recommended Gu Yangqian to oversee the Grand Canal; Cai argued and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel recommended Gu Yangqian to oversee the Grand Canal, Cai argued against the appointment and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 兵部將大敘平壤功，材力詆石星罔上，星乃不敢濫敘。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War was about to grant large rewards for the Pyongyang campaign; Cai forcefully denounced Shi Xing for deceiving his superiors, and Xing then did not dare to reward indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of War was preparing a major commendation for the Pyongyang campaign, Cai fiercely denounced Shi Xing for deceiving the throne, and Xing no longer dared to distribute rewards indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 其冬，復率同官言成憲不當為祭酒，馮夢禎不當為詹事，劉元震不當為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: That winter he again led his colleagues in saying that Cheng Xian should not be made director of the Imperial Academy, Feng Mengzhen should not be made junior mentor of the heir apparent, and Liu Yuanzhen should not be made vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he again led his colleagues in arguing that Cheng Xian should not be made director of the Imperial Academy, Feng Mengzhen should not be made junior mentor of the heir apparent, and Liu Yuanzhen should not be made vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝積前怒，言材屢借言事誣謗大臣，今復暗傷善類，乃貶三官，余停俸一歲。

translations.literal: The emperor, accumulating earlier anger, said Cai had repeatedly used memorializing to slander great ministers and now again covertly harmed worthy men; he therefore demoted three offices and suspended the salaries of the rest for one year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, nursing earlier grievances, declared that Cai had repeatedly used memorials to slander senior ministers and was now again covertly harming worthy men. He demoted three of them in rank and suspended the salaries of the rest for a year.

sentences.zh: 會御史崔景榮等論救，再貶程鄉典史。

translations.literal: When the censor Cui Jingrong and others petitioned in his defense, he was demoted again to archive clerk of Chengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor Cui Jingrong and others pleaded on his behalf, he was demoted again to archive clerk of Chengxiang.

sentences.zh: 材遂歸裏不出。

translations.literal: Cai then returned to his home district and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Cai then went home and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，始起尚寶丞，再遷太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was first recalled as assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then again promoted to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Cai was first recalled as assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then promoted again to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 還朝未幾，即乞歸。

translations.literal: Not long after returning to court he petitioned to go home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his return to court he petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，起南京通政使，卒。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he was recalled as commissioner of transmissions at Nanjing and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was recalled as commissioner of transmissions at Nanjing, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was posthumously granted the title of right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously ennobled as right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 朱吾弼，字諧卿，高安人。

translations.literal: Zhu Wubi, styled Xieqing, was a man of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wubi, whose courtesy name was Xieqing, came from Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授寧國推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 征授南京御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed a censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯弟學仕為南京工部主事，以贓敗。

translations.literal: The younger brother of Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao, Xueshi, served as a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and was ruined by corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhigao's younger brother Xueshi served as a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and was brought down by corruption.

sentences.zh: 南京刑部因誌臯故，輕其罪，議調饒州通判。

translations.literal: Because of Zhigao, the Nanjing Ministry of Justice lightened his crime and proposed transferring him to be vice prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zhigao's influence, the Nanjing Ministry of Justice softened his sentence and proposed transferring him to be vice prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 吾弼疏論，竟謫戍之。

translations.literal: Wubi memorialized in argument and in the end had him banished to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wubi memorialized against the leniency and ultimately secured his banishment to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 奏請建國本，簡閣臣，補言官，罷礦稅，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish the foundation of the state, simplify grand secretaries, fill the ranks of remonstrance officials, and abolish mining taxes; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to invest the crown prince, streamline the grand secretaries, fill vacant remonstrance posts, and abolish mining taxes—but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫魏允貞為稅使孫朝所訐，吾弼乞治朝欺罔罪。

translations.literal: The Shanxi grand coordinator Wei Yunzhen was impeached by the tax commissioner Sun Chao; Wubi begged that Chao be punished for deception.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shanxi grand coordinator Wei Yunzhen was impeached by the tax commissioner Sun Chao, Wubi petitioned that Chao be punished for deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 廣東稅使李鳳乾沒，奸人王遇桂請稅江南田契，吾弼皆疏論其罪。

translations.literal: The Guangdong tax commissioner Li Feng embezzled funds; the schemer Wang Yugui petitioned to tax land deeds in Jiangnan; Wubi memorialized on the crimes of all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong tax commissioner Li Feng had embezzled funds wholesale, and the schemer Wang Yugui petitioned to levy taxes on land deeds in Jiangnan. Wubi memorialized against the crimes of each.

sentences.zh: 時無賴子蜂起言利，廷臣輒連章力爭，帝雖不盡從，亦未嘗不容其切直。

translations.literal: At the time worthless men swarmed forth speaking of profit; court officials repeatedly submitted linked memorials arguing forcefully. Although the emperor did not fully follow them, he never failed to tolerate their blunt candor.
translations.idiomatic: Rascals were then swarming forth with schemes for profit, and court officials answered with linked memorials of fierce protest. The emperor did not always heed them, yet he never refused their blunt candor.

sentences.zh: 雷震皇陵，吾弼請帝廷見大臣，講求祖宗典制，次第舉行，與天下更始。

translations.literal: When thunder shook the imperial tombs, Wubi asked the emperor to receive great ministers in audience, study the ancestral institutions, carry them out in sequence, and make a fresh start with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder shook the imperial tombs, Wubi urged the emperor to receive his ministers in audience, recover the institutions of the ancestors, put them into practice step by step, and begin anew with the realm.

sentences.zh: 尋復言：「陛下孝敬疏於郊廟，惕厲弛於朝講；

translations.literal: Soon he again said: "Your Majesty's filial reverence is neglected regarding suburban temples and ancestral halls, and vigilance is relaxed at court lectures;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added, "Your Majesty's filial reverence has grown slack toward the suburban temples and ancestral halls, and your vigilance has loosened at court lectures;

sentences.zh: 土木盛宮苑，榛蕪遍殿廷，群小橫中外，正士困囹圄；

translations.literal: construction flourishes in the palace gardens, weeds overrun the halls and courts, petty men run rampant within and without, and upright gentlemen languish in prison;
translations.idiomatic: construction flourishes in the palace gardens while weeds overrun the halls and courts; petty men run rampant at court and beyond, and upright gentlemen languish in prison;

sentences.zh: 閭閻以礦稅竭，郵傳以輸免疲，流亡以水旱增，郡縣以征求困；

translations.literal: lanes and alleys are drained by mining taxes, the courier system is worn out by transport exemptions, exiles increase through flood and drought, and commanderies and counties are distressed by exactions;
translations.idiomatic: lanes and alleys are drained by mining taxes, the courier system is exhausted by transport exemptions, exiles multiply through flood and drought, and commanderies and counties are crushed by exactions;

sentences.zh: 草澤生心，衣冠喪氣；

translations.literal: the grasslands and marshes breed rebellious hearts, and the gentry lose their spirit;
translations.idiomatic: the countryside breeds rebellious hearts, and the gentry have lost their spirit;

sentences.zh: 公卿不能補牘，臺諫無從引裾。

translations.literal: grand secretaries cannot mend the ledgers, and censors and remonstrators have no way to seize the emperor's robe.
translations.idiomatic: grand secretaries cannot mend what is broken, and censors and remonstrators have no way to seize Your Majesty's robe.

sentences.zh: 不可不深察而改圖也。」

translations.literal: This cannot but be deeply examined and the plan changed.
translations.idiomatic: These matters cannot but be examined deeply and the course of state changed.

sentences.zh: 末言禮部侍郎郭正域疾惡嚴，居己峻，不可以楚事棄。

translations.literal: At the end he said that Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu hated evil sternly and held himself severely upright, and must not be abandoned on account of the Chu affair.
translations.idiomatic: He closed by saying that Guo Zhengyu, vice minister of rites, hated evil with stern rigor and held himself to a severe standard, and must not be cast aside because of the Chu affair.

sentences.zh: 先是，楚假王議起，首輔沈一貫陰左右王，以正域請行勘，嗾其黨錢夢臯阜輩逐之去。

translations.literal: Earlier, with the dispute over the supposed prince of Chu arising, Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan secretly sided with the prince. Because Zhengyu petitioned for an investigation, he incited his faction, Qian Menggao and others, to drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the controversy over the supposed prince of Chu arose, Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan had secretly favored the prince. Because Guo Zhengyu had petitioned for a formal investigation, Shen incited his allies Qian Menggao and others to drive him from office.

sentences.zh: 舉朝無敢留正域及言楚事者，吾弼獨抗章申理，而御史林秉漢以楚宗人戕殺巡撫，亦請詳勘。

translations.literal: The whole court dared not keep Zhengyu or speak of the Chu affair; Wubi alone submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, while the censor Lin Binghan, because a clansman of Chu had killed the grand coordinator, also petitioned for a detailed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: No one in court dared retain Guo Zhengyu or speak of the Chu affair, yet Wubi alone submitted a bold memorial in his defense. The censor Lin Binghan, noting that a clansman of Chu had murdered the grand coordinator, likewise petitioned for a thorough investigation.

sentences.zh: 且言：「王既非假，何憚於勘？」

translations.literal: He also said: "If the prince is not false, why fear an investigation?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If the prince is not an impostor, why fear an investigation?

sentences.zh: 吾弼、秉漢遂為一貫等所惡。

translations.literal: Wubi and Binghan were therefore hated by Yiguan and his party.
translations.idiomatic: Wubi and Binghan were therefore detested by Shen Yiguan and his allies.

sentences.zh: 會夢臯京察將黜，遂訐秉漢為正域鷹犬，語侵沈鯉、楊時喬、溫純。

translations.literal: When Menggao was about to be demoted in the capital evaluation, he then denounced Binghan as Zhengyu's hawk and hound, with language impugning Shen Li, Yang Shiqiao, and Wen Chun.
translations.idiomatic: When Menggao was about to be demoted in the capital evaluation, he denounced Binghan as Guo Zhengyu's henchman, and his language also impugned Shen Li, Yang Shiqiao, and Wen Chun.

sentences.zh: 秉漢坐貶貴州按察司檢校，而夢臯得留。

translations.literal: Binghan was demoted to archive clerk of the Guizhou surveillance commission, while Menggao was allowed to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Binghan was demoted to archive clerk of the Guizhou surveillance commission, while Menggao was permitted to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 郎中劉元珍論之，反獲譴。

translations.literal: The director Liu Yuanzhen spoke on the matter and in turn was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu Yuanzhen spoke up on the matter and was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 吾弼復疏直元珍，請黜夢臯，因力詆一貫，亦忤旨，停俸一年，遂移疾去。

translations.literal: Wubi again memorialized in defense of Yuanzhen, asked that Menggao be dismissed, and thereby fiercely denounced Yiguan; this too offended the throne, his salary was suspended for one year, and he then pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wubi memorialized again in Yuanzhen's defense, asked that Menggao be dismissed, and fiercely denounced Yiguan; this too offended the throne, his salary was suspended for a year, and he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 居三年，起南京光祿少卿，召為大理右丞。

translations.literal: After three years at home he was raised as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing and summoned as right vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three years at home he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing and summoned as right vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 齊、楚、浙三黨用事，吾弼復辭疾歸。

translations.literal: When the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions held power, Wubi again pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions held power, Wubi again pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，召還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended the throne, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong came to the throne, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he became minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年為御史吳裕中劾罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he was impeached and dismissed by the censor Wu Yuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi, Censor Wu Yuzhong impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 秉漢，字伯昭，長泰人。

translations.literal: Binghan, styled Bozhao, was a native of Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: Binghan, whose style was Bozhao, came from Changtai.

sentences.zh: 按廣東，亦再疏劾李鳳。

translations.literal: While touring Guangdong, he also twice memorialized impeaching Li Feng.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Guangdong as censor, he twice memorialized impeaching Li Feng.

sentences.zh: 既謫，尋移疾歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: After his banishment he soon pleaded illness and returned home, dying there.
translations.idiomatic: After his banishment he soon pleaded illness, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 張光前，字爾荷，澤州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangqian, styled Erhe, was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangqian, whose style was Erhe, came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授蒲圻知縣，補安肅。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Puqi and then transferred to Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Puqi and later transferred to Ansu.

sentences.zh: 甫四月，擢吏部驗封主事。

translations.literal: After only four months he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel's Seals and Investitures Section.
translations.idiomatic: After only four months he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel's Seals and Investitures Section.

sentences.zh: 歷文選員外郎、稽勛郎中。

translations.literal: He served as vice director in the Appointments Section and as director in the Merit Records Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director in the Appointments Section and as director in the Merit Records Section.

sentences.zh: 乞假去。

translations.literal: He asked for leave and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave and left office.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，趙南星為尚書，起為文選郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi, when Zhao Nanxing was minister, Guangqian was raised as director of the Appointments Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqi, when Zhao Nanxing became minister of Personnel, Guangqian was recalled as director of the Appointments Section.

sentences.zh: 甫視事，魏忠賢欲逐南星，假廷推謝應祥事矯旨切責。

translations.literal: As soon as he took office, Wei Zhongxian wished to drive Nanxing out; using the court nomination of Xie Yingxiang as a pretext, he forged an imperial rescript of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office, Wei Zhongxian sought to oust Nanxing and, using the court nomination of Xie Yingxiang as a pretext, forged an imperial rescript of sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 南星時與推應祥者，員外郎夏嘉遇，非光前也。

translations.literal: The one who had nominated Yingxiang with Nanxing at the time was the vice director Xia Jiayu, not Guangqian.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing's colleague in nominating Yingxiang had been Vice Director Xia Jiayu, not Guangqian.

sentences.zh: 光前抗疏爭之，曰：「南星人品事業昭灼人耳目，忽奉嚴旨責以不公忠，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: Guangqian submitted a forceful memorial contesting this, saying: "Nanxing's character and achievements are plain to all eyes; suddenly to receive a stern rescript charging him with partiality and disloyalty—I am privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqian submitted a forceful protest, writing: "Nanxing's character and achievements are plain for all to see; to receive a stern rescript charging him with partiality and disloyalty leaves me deeply perplexed.

sentences.zh: 選郎，諸曹領袖，尚書臂指，南星所甄別進退，臣實佐之。

translations.literal: The appointments director is the leader of all bureaus and the minister's right hand; in the promotions and dismissals Nanxing selected, your servant in fact assisted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments director leads all bureaus and serves as the minister's right hand; I in fact assisted in every promotion and dismissal Nanxing made.

sentences.zh: 功罪與共，乞先賜罷斥。」

translations.literal: Credit and blame should be shared; I beg to be dismissed first.
translations.idiomatic: Credit and blame should be shared; I beg that I be dismissed first.

sentences.zh: 亦被旨切責。

translations.literal: He too received an imperial rescript of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: He too received a sharp imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以推喬允升等代南星，忤忠賢意，削侍郎陳於廷及楊漣、左光鬥籍。

translations.literal: Before long, because he had nominated Qiao Yunsheng and others to replace Nanxing, offending Zhongxian, the vice ministers Chen Yuting and Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because he had nominated Qiao Yunsheng and others to replace Nanxing, offending Zhongxian, Vice Ministers Chen Yuting, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 光前又抗疏曰：「會推尚書，於廷主議，臣執筆，謹席稿待罪。」

translations.literal: Guangqian again submitted a forceful memorial saying: "In the joint nomination of a minister, Chen Yuting presided over the discussion and your servant held the brush; I respectfully await punishment with draft in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqian protested again: "In the joint nomination of a minister, Chen Yuting presided and I held the brush; I await punishment with the draft before me.

sentences.zh: 遂貶三秩，調外任。

translations.literal: He was then demoted three ranks and transferred to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted three ranks and transferred to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 光前操行清嚴，峻卻請謁。

translations.literal: Guangqian's conduct was pure and stern, and he sharply refused solicitations.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqian was pure and stern in conduct and firmly refused solicitations.

sentences.zh: 知縣石三畏贓私狼籍，得奧援，將授臺諫，光前出之為王官，其黨鹹側目。

translations.literal: The magistrate Shi Sanwei was flagrantly corrupt; with powerful backing he was about to be appointed to remonstrance office, but Guangqian posted him out as a princely attendant, and his faction glared with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shi Sanwei was flagrantly corrupt; with powerful backing he was about to receive a remonstrance appointment, but Guangqian posted him out as a princely attendant, to the resentment of his faction.

sentences.zh: 明年，光前兄右布政使光縉治兵遵化，為奄黨門克新所劾，亦削籍。

translations.literal: The next year Guangqian's elder brother Guangjin, right provincial administration commissioner, was training troops at Zunhua and was impeached by the eunuch faction's Men Kexin; he too was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his elder brother Guangjin, right provincial administration commissioner training troops at Zunhua, was impeached by the eunuch partisan Men Kexin and also struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並以忤奄去，見稱於世。

translations.literal: Both brothers left office for opposing the eunuchs and were praised by their age.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers left office for defying the eunuchs and were praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起光祿少卿，不赴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was raised as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments but declined.

sentences.zh: 三年，起太常。

translations.literal: In the third year he was raised to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 已，進大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 累疏乞休，及家而卒。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to retire and died after reaching home.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to retire and died after reaching home.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：朝政弛，則士大夫騰空言而少實用。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: When court governance slackens, scholar-officials soar in empty words and have little practical use.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: When court governance slackens, scholar-officials excel at empty words and achieve little in practice.

sentences.zh: 若陳邦瞻、畢懋康、翟鳳翀、董應舉，尚思有所建立，惜不逢明作之朝，故所表見止此耳。

translations.literal: Men such as Chen Bangzhan, Bi Maokang, Zhai Fengchong, and Dong Yingju still wished to accomplish something, but alas they did not meet a reign of enlightened achievement; therefore what they displayed stopped at this.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Chen Bangzhan, Bi Maokang, Zhai Fengchong, and Dong Yingju still sought to accomplish something, but they did not live in an age of enlightened governance; what they achieved was therefore limited.

sentences.zh: 蕭近高、洪文衡諸人皆以清素自矢，白瑜論鄭氏獄能持平，固卿貳之錚錚者歟。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingao, Hong Wenheng, and the others all held themselves to purity and integrity; Bai Yu, in judging the Zheng clan case, was able to remain impartial—were they not indeed the ringing voices among vice ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingao, Hong Wenheng, and the others held themselves to purity and integrity; Bai Yu judged the Zheng clan case with impartiality—they were indeed the clearest voices among the vice ministers.
